::: {.callout-note}
## About this page

This page **tests the panzoom extension** with the knitr graphics devices
and figure shapes used in practice: very wide collages (100 × 5 inches),
and webp, svg and pdf output. Every figure is marked with `#| panzoom: true`
and should open the pan/zoom viewer, except where a case says otherwise.

Cases with an expected opening view say so in their heading's
`expect-fit` attribute (`contain`, `height` or `width`), which the browser
test checks. By default (`fit: auto`) very wide figures open at screen
height from the left end, very tall ones at screen width from the top, and
everything else whole.

Cases with a `shift-scroll` attribute say which way Shift+scroll should
move the image: `x` (sideways), `y` (up and down) or `none` (it fits, so
it stays put); `zoomed-x` means sideways after zooming in until the image
extends past the screen both ways.

Cases with `expect-scale="1"` are smaller than the screen and must open
at their real size (1 image pixel per screen pixel), not enlarged, and
still zoom in.

webp comes from ragg's `agg_webp` device: knitr has no built-in webp
device, and `agg_webp` needs `units = "in"` because knitr passes sizes in
inches.
:::

```{r}
#| include: false
library(ragg)

# A collage: `n` panels side by side, like a wide patchwork figure.
collage <- function(n = 20) {
  set.seed(1)
  par(mfrow = c(1, n), mar = c(3, 3, 2, 1))
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    plot(cumsum(rnorm(200)), type = "l", main = paste("Panel", i),
         xlab = "", ylab = "", col = hcl.colors(n)[i], lwd = 2)
  }
}
```

## 1. Wide collage, png (100 × 5 in) {#c1 expect-fit="height" shift-scroll="x"}

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-width: 100
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-cap: "A 100 × 5 inch collage of 20 panels (png)."
collage()
```

## 2. Wide collage, webp (100 × 5 in) {#c2 expect-fit="height"}

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-width: 100
#| fig-height: 5
#| dev: agg_webp
#| fig-ext: webp
#| dev.args: !expr list(units = "in", res = 96)
#| fig-cap: "The same collage as webp."
collage()
```

## 3. Wide collage, svg (100 × 5 in) {#c3 expect-fit="height"}

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-width: 100
#| fig-height: 5
#| dev: svg
#| fig-cap: "The same collage as svg."
collage()
```

## 4. webp plot {#c4 expect-fit="contain" shift-scroll="none" expect-scale="1"}

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| dev: agg_webp
#| fig-ext: webp
#| dev.args: !expr list(units = "in", res = 96)
#| fig-cap: "A standard-size plot as webp."
filled.contour(volcano, color.palette = terrain.colors)
```

## 5. svg plot {#c5 expect-fit="contain" expect-scale="1"}

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| dev: svg
#| fig-cap: "A standard-size plot as svg."
filled.contour(volcano, color.palette = terrain.colors)
```

## 6. png + pdf (dev: [png, pdf]) {#c6 expect-fit="contain"}

Both files are written; the page shows the png.

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| dev: !expr c("png", "pdf")
#| fig-cap: "png shown, pdf written alongside."
filled.contour(volcano, color.palette = terrain.colors)
```

## 7. pdf only {#c7}

With only the pdf device, the HTML page has no bitmap to show; this case
records what the browser and panzoom do with it.

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| dev: pdf
#| fig-cap: "pdf only."
filled.contour(volcano, color.palette = terrain.colors)
```

## 8. Wide collage, webp at 2× resolution (100 × 5 in) {#c8}

At 192 dpi the collage is 19,200 px wide, beyond webp's limit of 16,383 px
per side; this case records what happens.

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-width: 100
#| fig-height: 5
#| dev: agg_webp
#| fig-ext: webp
#| dev.args: !expr list(units = "in", res = 192)
#| fig-cap: "The collage as webp at 192 dpi."
#| error: true
collage()
```

## 9. Wide collage with `fit: contain` {#c9 expect-fit="contain" shift-scroll="none"}

The override: the whole collage, as a strip.

```{r}
#| panzoom:
#|   fit: contain
#| fig-width: 100
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-cap: "The collage, forced to open whole."
collage()
```

## 10. Moderately wide figure (16 × 4 in) {#c10 expect-fit="contain"}

Wide, but readable whole: the size rule leaves it alone.

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-width: 16
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-cap: "A 4:1 figure."
collage(4)
```

## 11. Tall strip (4 × 60 in) {#c11 expect-fit="width" shift-scroll="y"}

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height: 60
#| fig-cap: "A tall strip of 15 panels."
set.seed(2)
par(mfrow = c(15, 1), mar = c(2, 3, 2, 1))
for (i in 1:15) plot(cumsum(rnorm(100)), type = "l", main = paste("Row", i), xlab = "", ylab = "")
```

## 12. Gallery of two collages {#c12 expect-fit="height"}

Left/Right and drags pan along the collage; PageDown, PageUp and the
buttons switch collages.

```{r}
#| panzoom:
#|   group: collages
#| fig-width: 100
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-cap:
#|   - "First collage."
#|   - "Second collage."
collage()
collage(25)
```

## 13. Large poster (24 × 18 in) {#c13 expect-fit="contain" shift-scroll="zoomed-x"}

Opens whole; zoomed in, it extends past the screen both ways, and
Shift+scroll moves sideways.

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-width: 24
#| fig-height: 18
#| fig-cap: "A 24 × 18 inch poster of 48 panels."
set.seed(3)
par(mfrow = c(6, 8), mar = c(2, 2, 2, 1))
for (i in 1:48) plot(cumsum(rnorm(100)), type = "l", main = paste("Panel", i), xlab = "", ylab = "")
```

## 14. Gallery of two tall strips {#c14 expect-fit="width"}

Each strip opens at screen width and extends downwards: Left/Right do
nothing (there is nowhere to go sideways) rather than switch strips;
PageDown, PageUp and the buttons switch.

```{r}
#| panzoom:
#|   group: strips
#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height: 60
#| fig-cap:
#|   - "First strip."
#|   - "Second strip."
for (k in 1:2) {
  set.seed(10 + k)
  par(mfrow = c(15, 1), mar = c(2, 3, 2, 1))
  for (i in 1:15) plot(cumsum(rnorm(100)), type = "l", main = paste("Strip", k, "row", i), xlab = "", ylab = "")
}
```

## 15. png + cairo_pdf (dev: [png, cairo_pdf]) {#c15 expect-fit="contain"}

Like case 6, with the cairo PDF device, which embeds fonts and handles
Unicode (µ, Greek letters) and transparency better than `pdf`. The page
shows the png either way; a PDF figure only ever appears as the browser's
PDF viewer (case 7), whichever device wrote it.

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| dev: !expr c("png", "cairo_pdf")
#| fig-cap: "png shown, cairo_pdf written alongside (µ = 5, α = 0.05)."
filled.contour(volcano, color.palette = terrain.colors,
               plot.title = title(main = "µ = 5, α = 0.05"))
```

## 16. Portrait photo {#c16 expect-fit="contain"}

An ordinary 9:16 photo is not a strip: it opens whole, on any screen width
(the test also checks this in a 2560 px wide window).

![A portrait photo.](../../images/mv-4.jpg){.panzoom width=30%}

## 17. Small plot (288 × 192 px) {#c17 expect-fit="contain" expect-scale="1"}

Opens at its real size, centered, rather than enlarged to fill the
screen; scroll still zooms in (up to `max-zoom`).

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-width: 3
#| fig-height: 2
#| fig-dpi: 48
#| fig-cap: "A small plot."
plot(pressure)
```
